residual_risk: The per-message `usage` shape is Claude Code's transcript format, not a documented contract; a future format change yields null (today's message) rather than a wrong number, but the usage line would quietly disappear.

Cache-rate defaults assume the published 1.25x write / 0.1x read multipliers on input, and one cache_write rate covers both the 5m and 1h cache TTLs, which are billed differently (1.25x vs 2x). Set cache_write explicitly to be exact; every figure is labelled an estimate either way.

Transcript turns count assistant messages, which is not `num_turns`'s definition from `claude -p`. They are kept in separate fields (spend.usage.turns vs num_turns / by_profile.turns) and never summed together.
Only exercised against Claude transcripts. A Copilot or Codex path landing in transcript_path would parse to null rather than usage.

`stats.rates` is a new board.json key read only by src/stats.js; loadBoard passes unknown keys through and doctor does not validate the schema, so nothing rejects it, but it is undocumented outside the code and the report's hint line.

results.summary:
hkb stats now reads spend off the session transcript when no harness reported one.

`priceOf` gained a third source under the run record and the worker log: the attempt's
`transcript_path` (the JSONL the Stop hook already records), summed per model and deduped by
message id — Claude Code writes one assistant message as several lines, each repeating the same
`usage`, so summing lines would bill a long turn four and five times over. The file is streamed a
chunk at a time through a StringDecoder, read only for an ended attempt that has no cheaper price,
once, always from disk and never over the network.

The report now names which of three things it is showing (`spend.basis`):
  reported  — `total_cost_usd` off the run record or the worker log
  estimate  — those tokens priced at the board's `stats.rates`, always written `~$…` and labelled
  usage     — turns and tokens, unpriced, which beat nothing

`total_usd` stays reported money only; estimates live in `estimated_usd`, so nothing can add the
two by accident.

hkb deliberately ships NO price table: a price it invented would look, in the output, exactly like
one Claude signed off on, and published prices move under a checkout that does not. Estimates come
from rates the board states, in .kanban/board.json:

  "stats": { "rates": { "claude-opus-5": { "input": 5, "output": 25 } } }

USD per million tokens; a key matches exactly, then as the longest prefix, then "default";
`cache_write`/`cache_read` are optional and fall back to the published 1.25x / 0.1x multipliers on
`input`. With no rates the report prints turns and tokens plus a one-line hint saying what to add.
A model that spent nothing is skipped when pricing — Claude Code files an interrupted turn under
the model `<synthetic>` with every counter at zero, and one of those must not cost a board its
estimate.

A missing or unreadable transcript (a board reported from a host that never ran the attempt)
degrades to exactly the message that was there before, never an error.

Verified against a real 190-turn transcript on this host: a board that used to print "not recorded
on any of the 1 worker attempt" now prints 190 turns, 160k output tokens, 674k cache writes, 38M
cache reads — and ~$26.97 ESTIMATED once rates are set.

For the next worker: `stats.rates` is documented only in the code and in the hint line the report
prints; a README / docs/ mention would be worth having, and was out of this task's file scope.
`src/hook.js` and `src/model.js`'s SESSION_FIELDS were left untouched — they belong to #115's
sibling, which only widens which attempts carry `transcript_path`. Draft PR: #123.
